Every state where this registry lists a DataBank facility, Utah, Virginia, Texas, California, and Nevada, matches a market named on the company own site. No founding date, headquarters address, ownership structure, or acquisition history, and no building specific address or individual MW figures for this particular registry row, were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
DataBank SLC5 in Bluffdale, Utah, publishes 10 MW of IT capacity across 49,180 square feet of technical space, operated by DataBank.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 1000 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 250 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DataBank SLC5. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Utah has 9 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 8 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 51.69 MW. DataBank SLC5 contributes 10 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
